narrator: Dr. Seward (letter and diary), Lucy Westenra (diary)
summary: Seward meets Van Helsing at Liverpool Street and they go to Hillingham, where they find Lucy near death from lack of blood. Arthur arrives unexpectedly and gives blood in a direct transfusion after Lucy is given a narcotic; Lucy revives. Van Helsing glimpses two punctures over her external jugular vein when her velvet throat-band slips, and goes to Amsterdam while Seward keeps watch; Lucy sleeps peacefully. On 9 September Seward falls asleep on the sofa, and by morning Lucy is drained again; Seward gives a second transfusion with a morphia injection. Van Helsing forbids telling Arthur and takes over the nightwatch. On 11 September a parcel of garlic flowers from Haarlem arrives: Van Helsing rubs garlic on the windows, door jamb and fireplace, latches the windows and makes a garlic wreath for Lucy's neck, forbidding her to open the window or door.

scenes.title: Liverpool Street: the husbandman's corn
scenes.summary: Van Helsing tells Seward to keep knowledge to himself, compares his silence to a husbandman who does not dig up planted corn, and urges Seward to keep careful case notes.
scenes.key_quote: Nothing is too small. I counsel you, put down in record even your doubts and surmises.

scenes.title: Lucy found near death
scenes.summary: Lucy is chalky pale, lips and gums bloodless, breathing laboured. Van Helsing declares she needs a transfusion at once.
scenes.key_quote: She will die for sheer want of blood to keep the heart's action as it should be.

scenes.title: First transfusion (Arthur)
scenes.summary: Arthur arrives; Van Helsing recruits him. Lucy drinks a narcotic, Arthur kisses her, and Van Helsing transfuses blood without defibrinating it. Colour returns to Lucy.
scenes.key_quote: Then with swiftness, but with absolute method, Van Helsing performed the operation.

scenes.title: The marks on the throat
scenes.summary: The black velvet band with a diamond buckle slips, revealing a red mark. Seward loosens it and finds two small punctures with white, worn edges over the external jugular vein.
scenes.key_quote: Just over the external jugular vein there were two punctures, not large, but not wholesome-looking.

scenes.title: Seward's vigil
scenes.summary: Van Helsing leaves for Amsterdam. Lucy fears sleep but trusts Seward's promise and sleeps peacefully all night.
scenes.key_quote: Afraid to go to sleep! Why so?

scenes.title: Seward sleeps; Lucy drained again
scenes.location: Hillingham, adjoining room then Lucy's bedroom
scenes.summary: Lucy talks Seward into resting on a sofa in the next room with both doors open. In the morning Van Helsing finds her swooned and nearly bloodless.
scenes.key_quote: All our work is undone; we must begin again.

scenes.title: Second transfusion (Seward)
scenes.summary: Brandy is used to revive her, then Seward gives blood with a morphia injection to keep Lucy asleep. Van Helsing insists Arthur must not know.
scenes.key_quote: Mind, nothing must be said of this.

scenes.title: The garlic flowers
scenes.summary: A parcel of garlic flowers from Haarlem arrives. Van Helsing rubs them on windows, door jamb and fireplace, latches the windows, and puts a wreath round Lucy's neck.

creatures.name: Unseen bloodsucker (the vampire)
creatures.description: Not seen; leaves two punctures over Lucy's jugular with white worn edges.
creatures.behaviour: Feeds on Lucy at night while she sleeps; strikes again the night Seward sleeps.
creatures.quote: two punctures, not large, but not wholesome-looking

vampire_lore.rule: Two puncture wounds on the neck over the jugular
vampire_lore.detail: Edges white and worn as if by trituration; little visible blood loss on the bed.
vampire_lore.quote: the edges were white and worn-looking, as if by some trituration

vampire_lore.detail: Rubbed on sashes, door jamb and fireplace so every breath of air carries garlic; also worn as wreath. Van Helsing hints it is a spell to keep out an evil spirit.

vampire_lore.rule: Victim's sleep is where the weakness occurs
vampire_lore.detail: Lucy's weakness comes in sleep and she fears it; a watched night passes safely.
vampire_lore.quote: All this weakness comes to me in sleep

vampire_lore.rule: Victims must be kept sealed in room: no open window or door
vampire_lore.detail: The visitor enters via window (earlier scratching), so garlic and latches block it.
vampire_lore.quote: do not to-night open the window or the door.

vampire_lore.detail: Arthur's blood only partly restored her, and it was gone by the next morning.
vampire_lore.quote: All our work is undone; we must begin again.

puzzles.name: Hidden throat marks
puzzles.setup: A velvet band hides the cause of Lucy's blood loss.
puzzles.obstacle: Discover the cause without alarming others.
puzzles.book_solution: Van Helsing sees the red mark when the band is dragged up; Seward loosens the band and examines the punctures.
puzzles.game_idea: Examine-inspect puzzle: move the band without waking Lucy, then compare puncture spacing against a clue card.
puzzles.quote: The velvet band again covered the red mark.

puzzles.name: Seal the bedroom
puzzles.setup: A visitor enters Lucy's room at night.
puzzles.book_solution: Latch the windows, rub garlic on sashes, door jamb and fireplace, and hang a garlic wreath.
puzzles.game_idea: Room-sealing puzzle: find all entries (window, door, chimney) and ward each within a limited quantity of garlic.
puzzles.quote: he rubbed them all over the sashes, as though to ensure that every whiff of air that might get in would be laden with the garlic smell

puzzles.name: Who gives blood?
puzzles.setup: Lucy needs a transfusion; donors differ in strength.
puzzles.obstacle: Pick the donor and keep it secret from Mrs. Westenra and Arthur.
puzzles.book_solution: Seward volunteers, Arthur supplants him; later Seward gives blood and takes only a measured amount.
puzzles.game_idea: Resource-management: donor health bars limit how much can be transfused each night.
puzzles.quote: You took a great deal more from Art.
